message.content:
**Answer** One of the most celebrated and widely recognized sculptures of the 19th century is **“The Kiss” (Le Baiser)** by **Auguste Rodin**, completed in 1889. It epitomizes the era’s shift toward expressive, emotionally charged realism and has become an icon of modern sculpture. --- ### Why “The Kiss” stands out | Feature | Details | |---------|---------| | **Artist** | Auguste Rodin (1840‑1917) | | **Date** | 1889 (first cast) | | **Style** | Realist/Impressionist; early modernism | | **Material** | Bronze (originally marble) | | **Subject** | A passionate embrace between two lovers | | **Impact** | • Challenged traditional academic norms.
• Influenced generations of sculptors.
• Became a symbol of romantic love in popular culture. | --- ### Other notable 19th‑century sculptures | Sculpture | Artist | Year | Significance | |-----------|--------|------|--------------| | **The Gates of Hell** | Rodin | 1880‑1890 (unfinished) | Monumental, narrative work exploring human emotion. | | **The Thinker** | Rodin | 1902 (post‑century) | Though technically early 20th, it’s often grouped with late‑19th works. | | **The Statue of Liberty** | Frédéric Bartholdi | 1886 | Iconic national monument, not a “portrait” but a monumental sculpture. | | **The Winged Victory of Samothrace** | Ancient Greek (recast 19th c.) | 2nd century BCE (recast 19th c.) | Reintroduced classical ideals to the era. | --- ### Bottom line If you’re looking for a single sculpture that captures the spirit and artistic innovation of the 19th century, **Rodin’s “The Kiss”** is the most frequently cited and celebrated example. It remains a staple in museums worldwide and continues to inspire both artists and the public alike.
